items.heading: The Logic Behind the Push
items.text: The logic behind the push is straightforward. A huge number of students move from class 10 into a stream choice, and later from class 12 into a course and college choice, with very little structured decision support otherwise.

items.heading: This Is the Part That
items.text: This is the part that rarely gets said plainly. A single school counsellor, when a school has one at all in a dedicated role rather than a teacher carrying it as extra duty, is very often responsible for several hundred students spread across multiple grades. Counselling is frequently not even their primary job; it sits on top of a full teaching timetable.

items.heading: A Guidance
items.text: A guidance-and-counselling cell , usually staffed by a teacher given counselling as an additional responsibility, occasionally by a dedicated trained counsellor in larger or better-resourced schools.

items.heading: Periodic Career
items.text: Periodic career-guidance sessions , often batch-wise for an entire section or grade rather than one student at a time.

items.heading: Psychometric or Aptitude
items.text: Psychometric or aptitude-based assessment tools , pushed in various cycles particularly around the classes 9-12 window when stream and course decisions are closing in.

items.heading: Alumni or Industry
items.text: Alumni or industry-interaction sessions , where former students or working professionals talk about a field, more as awareness-building than individualized advice.
